newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico ruling party, labor fearful of opposition.
newsitem.headline: Mexico ruling party, labor fearful of opposition.

text.p: A powerful pro-government labour confederation and a leader of Mexico's ruling party secretly have expressed fears that opposition parties could oust the ruling party from power, newspapers reported Tuesday.

The Confederation of Mexican Workers (CTM) and the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) also began planning a blitz by the 5 million CTM workers to get out the vote for congressional elections on July 6, leaders said in a private meeting tape-recorded by at least two newspapers.
The PRI has ruled Mexico with a firm hand for 67 years.
The meeting was on Monday between PRI Secretary General Juan S. Millan and the CTM, led by the 96-year-old Fidel Velazquez, a key instrument in PRI control over labour for more than half a century.
"There is discouragement among members of our party (as if) we are heading, inexorably, toward an electoral defeat," Millan said, according to the Mexico City daily La Jornada.
La Jornada and the competing newspapaper Reforma reported excerpts from the meeting in Tuesday's editions.

La Jornada is linked with the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) while Reforma has ties to the conservative National Action Party (PAN). They are the two strongest opposition parties in Mexico.
Millan seemed more concerned with the PAN, saying it was "better organised," La Jornada reported.

"There will be a tactic and different strategies oriented toward getting the fellow workers to vote for the PRI," Velazquez said, adding that the CTM would concentrate on gubernatorial races in states held by the opposition.
"It's preferable to dissolve the CTM before supporting a government of the opposition," he told reporters.
